verses.text: Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,

“Go, and proclaim in the ears of Jerusalem, saying, ‘Yahweh says, “I remember for you the kindness of your youth, the love of your weddings; how you went after me in the wilderness, in a land that was not sown.
Israel was holiness to Yahweh, the first fruits of his increase. All who devour him shall be held guilty. Evil shall come on them,”’ says Yahweh.”
Hear Yahweh’s word, O house of Jacob, and all the families of the house of Israel!
Yahweh says, “What unrighteousness have your fathers found in me, that they have gone far from me, and have walked after worthless vanity, and have become worthless?

They didn’t say, ‘Where is Yahweh who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, who led us through the wilderness, through a land of deserts and of pits, through a land of drought and of the shadow of death, through a land that no one passed through, and where no man lived?’
I brought you into a plentiful land, to eat its fruit and its goodness; but when you entered, you defiled my land, and made my heritage an abomination.

The priests didn’t say, ‘Where is Yahweh?’ and those who handle the law didn’t know me. The rulers also transgressed against me, and the prophets prophesied by Baal, and followed things that do not profit.
“Therefore I will yet contend with you,” says Yahweh, “and I will contend with your children’s children.
For pass over to the islands of Kittim, and see; and send to Kedar, and consider diligently; and see if there has been such a thing.
Has a nation changed its gods, which really are no gods? But my people have changed their glory for that which does not profit.
“Be astonished, you heavens, at this, and be horribly afraid. Be very desolate,” says Yahweh.
“For my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the spring of living waters, and cut them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.
Is Israel a slave? Is he born into slavery? Why has he become a captive?
The young lions have roared at him, and yelled. They have made his land waste. His cities are burned up, without inhabitant.
The children also of Memphis and Tahpanhes have broken the crown of your head.
“Haven’t you brought this on yourself, in that you have forsaken Yahweh your God,  when he led you by the way?
Now what do you gain by going to Egypt, to drink the waters of the Shihor? Or why do you to go on the way to Assyria, to drink the waters of the River?

“Your own wickedness will correct you, and your backsliding will rebuke you. Know therefore and see that it is an evil and bitter thing, that you have forsaken Yahweh your God, and that my fear is not in you,” says the Lord, Yahweh of Armies.
“For long ago I broke off your yoke, and burst your bonds. You said, ‘I will not serve;’ for on every high hill and under every green tree you bowed yourself, playing the prostitute.
Yet I had planted you a noble vine, a pure and faithful seed. How then have you turned into the degenerate branches of a foreign vine to me?
For though you wash yourself with lye, and use much soap, yet your iniquity is marked before me,” says the Lord Yahweh.
“How can you say, ‘I am not defiled. I have not gone after the Baals’? See your way in the valley. Know what you have done. You are a swift dromedary traversing her ways;

a wild donkey used to the wilderness, that sniffs the wind in her craving. When she is in heat, who can turn her away? All those who seek her will not weary themselves. In her month, they will find her.
“Keep your feet from being bare, and your throat from thirst. But you said, ‘It is in vain. No, for I have loved strangers, and I will go after them.’
As the thief is ashamed when he is found, so is the house of Israel ashamed; they, their kings, their princes, and their priests, and their prophets;

who tell wood, ‘You are my father;’ and a stone, ‘You have given birth to me:’ for they have turned their back to me, and not their face; but in the time of their trouble they will say, ‘Arise, and save us.’
“But where are your gods that you have made for yourselves? Let them arise, if they can save you in the time of your trouble: for you have as many gods as you have towns, O Judah.
“Why will you contend with me? You all have transgressed against me,” says Yahweh.
“I have struck your children in vain. They received no correction. Your own sword has devoured your prophets, like a destroying lion.
Generation, consider Yahweh’s word. Have I been a wilderness to Israel? Or a land of thick darkness? Why do my people say, ‘We have broken loose. We will come to you no more?’
“Can a virgin forget her ornaments, or a bride her attire? Yet my people have forgotten me for days without number.
How well you prepare your way to seek love! Therefore you have even taught the wicked women your ways.
Also the blood of the souls of the innocent poor is found in your skirts. You did not find them breaking in; but it is because of all these things.
“Yet you said, ‘I am innocent. Surely his anger has turned away from me.’ “Behold, I will judge you, because you say, ‘I have not sinned.’
Why do you go about so much to change your ways? You will be ashamed of Egypt also, as you were ashamed of Assyria.
You will also leave that place with your hands on your head; for Yahweh has rejected those in whom you trust, and you won’t prosper with them.

footnotes.content: The Lord speaks. He always does, but we so often fail to listen. Here, even amid Israel's drift, His word still comes—not because they deserve it, but because He is faithful when His children are not.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I remember—what a word from the Lord. He holds the wilderness journey in His memory: Israel's fresh love, their trust when they followed Him into the desert with nothing but His promise. We forget our best moments with Him far too quickly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Holy to the Lord—the first fruits, set apart and precious. Israel was meant to be His sign to all nations. When we are unfaithful to Him, we lose not just our own blessing, but our calling to show others His goodness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hear the Lord's word. The call itself is mercy—He invites them to listen before judging. But listening means stopping our chatter, our justifications, and letting His voice break through our noise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: What wrong did I do? The Lord's question cuts: He gave everything, yet they still left. We often complain about life's hardship, forgetting that the greatest hurt comes when we walk away from the One who loves us best.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The wilderness journey—it was no accident they didn't ask where He was. They simply forgot. The Lord led them through death-shadow lands, and they learned to trust. Yet when the way grew hard or long, they abandoned that hard-won knowledge.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I brought you to plenty—and they defiled it. This is the tragedy of abundance without gratitude: we receive good gifts and treat them carelessly, as though we earned them. The land was never theirs to desecrate; it was always the Lord's.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even the priests—the guardians of knowledge—forgot to ask where He was. This is how corruption spreads: not all at once, but quietly, as those who should remember become the first to forget. Leaders who lose their own hunger for God mislead everyone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will contend with your children's children. Sin echoes through generations; the wounds we inherit are real. Yet this is also His warning: turn now, lest your choices bind those who come after you to the same hard path.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Look to Kittim and Kedar—distant lands of other peoples. The Lord invites an honest comparison: Show me another nation so disloyal, so willing to abandon their gods. The shame is not in exile but in the proof of their own foolishness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Nations keep their false gods, holding fast to empty names. But Israel traded their glory—the living God—for things that profit nothing. How strange: the unfaithful gods are clung to while the true One is abandoned.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Be astonished, you heavens. Even creation recoils from such faithlessness. The earth and sky are summoned as witnesses to Israel's unthinkable betrayal, as if all of nature cries out: How could you do this to Him?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Forsaken living water, cut out broken cisterns. The image is perfect: they abandoned the spring that never runs dry for containers that leak and fail. We do the same when we chase comfort, status, or numbing over His constant presence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Is Israel a slave? The question stings with irony: born free under His covenant, yet they made themselves slaves to folly. True slavery is not what's done to us but what we do to ourselves when we choose anything over His freedom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Young lions roared—enemies destroyed the land. When we abandon God's protection, we leave ourselves exposed. The world's powers move swiftly against those who stand alone, unshielded by the Lord's hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Memphis and Tahpanhes—Egypt's great cities—broke the crown of Judah's head. Israel once sought Egypt's protection instead of trusting the Lord; now Egypt's princes strip them bare. Alliances built on doubt always collapse.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Haven't you brought this on yourself? The hard word is true: we are not just victims of circumstance. When we leave His leading, we walk into the pain we create. Taking responsibility—not just blame, but true seeing—is where healing begins.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Why go to Egypt, to Assyria, to drink strange waters? The Lord points to their own restless seeking: running from ally to ally, from power to power, never satisfied, never trusting. Thirst that never finds its well.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Your own wickedness will correct you—a bitter teacher. The Lord doesn't always need to strike; our own choices rise up and rebuke us. There is no fear of the Lord left in them, and without that fear, there is only the harsh instruction of consequence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I broke off your yoke—freedom already given. Yet they said, I will not serve, and bound themselves to idols on every high place. This is the paradox of rebellion: we refuse the Lord's easy yoke only to take on ten heavier ones.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A noble vine, pure seed—Israel was planted by God's own hand with care and hope. How then become degenerate, foreign branches? The question hangs: when something starts so good, how do we let it rot? What kills the noble vine we once were?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wash yourself with lye and soap—it will not help. Sin leaves a mark before the Lord that no scrubbing erases. Only repentance, sincere turning, washes that stain away. We can polish ourselves endlessly and remain spotted.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: How can you say, I am not defiled? The swift dromedary image is sharp: they race after idols with urgent hunger. Denial is the final blindness—we convince ourselves we are not lost even as we rush toward the cliff.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A wild donkey in heat, sniffing the wind—the image is raw and unflinching. Israel pursued idolatry with the mindless urgency of animal craving. When reason is drowned out by appetite, all wisdom flees.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Keep your feet, keep your throat—the Lord offers boundaries, mercy even in warning. But they said, It is in vain. They rejected His care as useless and chose their own path to ruin, eyes wide open.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: As the thief is ashamed when found—shame comes to all who built on falsehood. Kings, princes, priests, prophets all fall together. When the foundation is rotten, the whole house tumbles, and none escape the shame.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They tell wood, You are my father; and stone, You have given birth to me. The absurdity stings: they beg carved wood and shaped rock for salvation. Then in trouble, they cry, Arise and save us—forgetting who alone can hear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Where are your gods that you have made? Let them arise and save you. The challenge is cruel and true: in the moment of need, all the false comfort crumbles. The gods we fashioned cannot deliver.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Why will you contend with me? The Lord asks the bewildering question: Why argue? Why debate? The evidence is plain. They have transgressed. At some point, further protest becomes its own blindness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I have struck your children in vain—discipline that bore no fruit. The Lord tried to teach, but they refused to learn. A parent's deepest sorrow: to see judgment fail to turn a child's heart homeward.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Have I been a wilderness to Israel? The question is tender under its edge: Did I abandon you? Am I the problem? No—yet they say so, blind to all His provision. Ingratitude rewrites history in the heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A virgin forget her ornaments, a bride her attire? The tender image breaks: we remember what we treasure, hold what matters close. Yet Israel has forgotten the Lord for days without number, as if He were never their joy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: How well you prepare your way to seek love! The path of idolatry is well-worn—they have become skilled in it, even teaching the wicked women their ways. Sin begets skill, and the skilled sinner leads others astray.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The blood of innocent poor on your skirts—their hands are stained. Idolatry is not neutral; it feeds injustice. When we lose the fear of the Lord, we lose the barrier that protects the helpless.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I am innocent—the last refuge of the hard heart. We declare ourselves blameless even as the Lord prepares to judge. This is the deepest sin: not just unfaithfulness, but the refusal to see, the insistence on innocence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Why do you go about so much to change your ways? They run from power to power—Egypt, Assyria—seeking a fix for the unfixable. The only change that saves is the turning of the heart; all other motion is just running.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You will leave with hands on your head—the posture of despair and shame. Readers today hear an echo in every failed scheme we trust and every alliance we build on sand instead of on Him. When we reject His care, we are left defenseless, hands empty and hearts broken.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
